Resolves #22021

A keyboard-focused Button now shows a two-pixel outline with a contrasting inset band. Both bands sit inside the button so clipped toolbars keep the indicator visible. The same rule serves the Theme Switcher, and forced-colors mode uses a system outline.

Evidence: L3 actual keyboard and pointer modality, forced colors and rendered workbench comparison in headless Chromium → L3 required.

CI jobs: +0.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Tab focused real default, pressed-primary and ghost buttons in each of the five bundled themes. The shared rule painted the solid outline and neutral band. |
| AC-2 | A real Grid header inside its overflow-hidden toolbar reported the inward outline in both Neo themes. Pointer-restored focus retained its existing outline treatment, and the first keydown restored the indicator. In forced colors the system outline remained visible. |
| AC-3 | The Button component test now asserts the indicator after re-enabling a control. Its preceding Tab still skips the disabled control. The workbench comparison is below. |

## Deltas from ticket

The Theme Switcher inherits the shared indicator, and its forced-color glyph treatment remains in place.

## Test Evidence

All 51 Button and dock-rail component tests passed, along with the five dock-rail layering unit tests. The second commit expresses native keyboard focus and Neo’s keyboard marker as separate selector arms, so the stylesheet guard reads both complete selectors.

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #22021 (ACs, `Design authority:` WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7), my own measurement behind defect-note `d80e4388` (Tab onto a button: `:focus-visible` matched, computed outline `none`, box-shadow `none`, in Neo Dark and Neo Light), `resources/css/src/button/Base.css` (`&:focus {outline: var(--button-outline-active)}`) and the five theme files that set the token to `none`.

One rule with token plus system-colour fallbacks, two selector arms (native `:focus-visible` and Neo's `.neo-focus-keyboard` marker, both excluding `.neo-focus-pointer`), an inset placement that survives clipping, a forced-colors arm, and the Button spec asserts style, width and offset after Tab.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: Classic Light, classic Dark and Cyberpunk define neither `--sem-color-border-focus` nor `--sem-color-surface-neutral-default`, and buttons run with `color-scheme: normal` (`--neo-color-scheme` only reaches Select and Progress). So those themes take the light-scheme fallbacks. Measured at `4c135fd49a` on `examples/button/base` in classic Dark: outline `2px rgb(0, 0, 0)`, inset band `rgb(255, 255, 255)` on a `rgb(60, 63, 65)` button. That is a white frame inside a dark button: plainly visible, so AC-1 holds, but it is not that theme's palette. A token pair in each classic theme would fix it, or `color-scheme: var(--neo-color-scheme)` on the button. That's a follow-up, not this PR. I also checked whether replacing `box-shadow` on focus drops a shadow some button relies on: `button/Base.css` sets none.
